=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's package.** The "market context" preamble and the assertion that positions are "FINAL" and "settled at principal level" are the Seller's advocacy, not facts. Please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed; nothing in our instructions records such an agreement. Note also that the Disclosure Letter is markedly more candid than the Seller Update: it confirms the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment/assignment and incident investigation are all *not* done. Our mark-up should hold the Seller to the Disclosure Letter facts, not the Update's gloss.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), presented as top of "market range".
- Buyer wants: materially higher – open at 100% of price, land no lower than ~50% (AUD 12m); fundamental/title/tax/specific indemnities at 100% and outside this cap.
- Recommendation: Reject 20%; counter at 100% with a fallback to 50%. *Reason: a 20% cap plus a 1% deductible basket means a single significant warranty breach in a business with Bluefen (30% revenue) and an open data incident is largely uninsured by the Seller; alternatively consider W&I insurance to bridge.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 basket; **deductible** (only excess recoverable).
- Buyer wants: de minimis ~AUD 10,000; basket ~0.5% (AUD 120,000) and **tipping** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims arising from the same facts aggregated for both thresholds; thresholds not applying to fundamental, tax or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: Accept basket concept only if tipping and aggregation are included; reduce both figures. *Reason: a deductible basket is a hidden 1% price reduction, and without aggregation the three Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k) could be argued to fall short of the basket.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months; plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covers at least one full audit cycle and the FY27 accounts); and the default reversed – limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: Counter at 24 months; delete the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: the default rule silently exports the 18-month/20% regime to tax, title and indemnity claims (see N-014).*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – cap at 100% of price, 6–7 year period (or no limit), no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure.
- Recommendation: Reject outright. *Reason: if title fails the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; recovering a maximum of AUD 4.8m within 18 months is not a commercial outcome and is well below any market norm.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cll 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: express carve-out from every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or Company management.
- Recommendation: Insist; non-negotiable. *Reason: a clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud is unlikely to be enforced in NSW, but its absence invites argument and the non-reliance clause as drafted would also undermine misleading-conduct claims.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all public records.
- Buyer wants: disclosure limited to matters "fairly disclosed" in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no general disclosure of the data room or public searches; disclosures made against specific warranties.
- Recommendation: Reject general disclosure; accept only the specific disclosures in sections 2–10, each tightened. *Reason: data-room-wide disclosure converts every warranty into a representation that the Buyer found everything itself, which is the opposite of the purpose of warranties.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller (cl 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, or that was **discoverable** from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete; at most, limited to the *actual* knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals of matters specifically set out in the Disclosure Letter; no adviser or constructive knowledge.
- Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3. *Reason: "discoverable" is constructive knowledge and, combined with N-006, would make the warranties practically unclaimable.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue)**
- Seller: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of any written consent. Disclosure Letter admits no consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent (waivable by Buyer only) requiring Bluefen's written, unconditional consent in a form approved by the Buyer, together with evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; warranty of no termination/renegotiation repeated at Completion; price-adjustment or walk right if not obtained by the long-stop date.
- Recommendation: Make it a hard CP. *Reason: loss of 30% of revenue post-Completion cannot be cured by a capped warranty claim.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)**
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion".
- Buyer wants: the deal is debt-free/cash-free – facility repaid at Completion from the purchase price per a payout letter; executed deed of release and discharge of all security (including PPSR releases and any share mortgage) delivered **at** Completion as a completion deliverable; amount itemised in the funds flow.
- Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release. *Reason: the Buyer would otherwise acquire a company carrying AUD 3.2m of debt and live security with no mechanism to recover it from the Seller.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (AUD 420k)**
- Seller: "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/debt-like items deducted from the price (or paid by the Seller through payroll at Completion); grossed-up amounts itemised in the funds flow; specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Recommendation: Deduct from price with indemnity. *Reason: these are triggered by Completion, payable by the Company, and silently shift ~AUD 420k+ of cost onto the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (AUD 180k open; SOW3 IP conditional on payment)**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate".
- Buyer wants: payment of the AUD 180k and a confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials from Ironquay as a condition/completion deliverable; a specific indemnity covering all loss from any failure of title to the SOW3 IP (not just the fee), outside the cap, basket and general time limits; an IP ownership warranty not qualified by disclosure of this issue.
- Recommendation: Fix before Completion, backed by full indemnity. *Reason: under cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 materials until payment clears – an AUD 180k indemnity does not cover the value of IP the business may be using.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (~1,240 records)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material; disclosed but with no breach characterisation or loss figure.
- Buyer wants: completed investigation (access confirmed/excluded, scope, Notifiable Data Breach assessment under the Privacy Act) before Completion; any required OAIC/individual notifications made pre-Completion; specific indemnity for all losses, regulatory penalties, notification costs and customer claims, outside cap/basket/time limits; warranty of no other incidents.
- Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion closure. *Reason: a notifiable breach involving customer personal information carries regulatory and customer-contract exposure (including with Bluefen) that is unquantified and should sit entirely with the Seller.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Buyer wants: confirmation whether each is committed, terminable or accrued and when; if committed pre-Completion and not reflected in working capital/accounts, treat as debt-like or leakage; related-claims aggregation (see N-002).
- Recommendation: Request the contracts and treat as a price-adjustment item unless shown to be budgeted ordinary course. *Reason: the split into three identical amounts and the Disclosure Letter's refusal to say they are ordinary course suggest they may be structured around the thresholds.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single regime for all Claims; limitations apply to everything unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: distinct, clearly drafted regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title, (iii) tax, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, incident, Sandbar), (v) fraud – each with its own cap, thresholds and period, and the specific indemnities expressly outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers.
- Recommendation: Redraft cl 12–13 on a schedule-by-category basis. *Reason: the Seller's default rule is the mechanism by which every bespoke protection in N-004 to N-012 would be collapsed back into 20%/18 months.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title "evidenced by" the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter concedes the Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: own verification before signing – ASIC company extract, share certificate(s), review of any share mortgage/PPSR registrations (particularly Riverlark security), board minutes approving transfer; fundamental warranties of legal and beneficial ownership free of encumbrances; delivery of transfer, certificates and register update at Completion.
- Recommendation: Do not rely on the Seller's register; run the searches now. *Reason: the register is a Company-maintained document and is not evidence that the shares are unencumbered.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime" (20% / 18 months / disclosure / knowledge qualifiers).
- Buyer wants: a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, no cap other than price, 7 years, not subject to disclosure or knowledge); tax warranties on the same basis; IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source, employee/contractor assignments) with a higher cap and 3-year period and specifically not qualified by the Ironquay disclosure.
- Recommendation: Treat as open and table buyer-form tax indemnity and IP warranties. *Reason: for a SaaS business the IP is the asset being bought, and tax exposures routinely surface beyond 18 months.*

---

**Other items to pick up in the mark-up (not on your list):** DD-007 office lease – confirm the notification is given pre-Completion as a Seller covenant; DD-009 Mossvale – confirm by review of the clause (not the Seller's characterisation) that a share sale does not trigger the assignment restriction, and obtain a comfort letter if ambiguous.

**Overall:** the package should not be accepted as "fair and balanced". Priority order for the counter: N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), N-008 (Bluefen CP), N-014/N-004/N-005 (separate regimes and fraud), N-006/N-007 (disclosure and knowledge), then quantum items (N-001, N-002, N-003, N-010–N-013, N-016).
